visual_direction: A cobalt-blue hoop rolls through a restrained stone-and-brass observatory. The wide central opening is always legible, with an intentionally framed stationary brass crossover visible through it before the gate sequence.

render_scope.camera_grammar: low-angle rolling follow; one continuous exterior shot

route_and_camera.route: C2 exposed rail: release [-4.55,-1.15,3.10], S-bend trigger [-0.78,0.05,2.36], gate threshold [0.55,0.40,2.04], broad descending curve [2.10,1.20,1.32], lower cradle [3.72,1.78,0.86]. Minimum centerline radius 3.10 m; bank magnitude never exceeds 12 degrees.
route_and_camera.central_hole_composition: At 1.75-2.20 s, frame the fixed crossover rail 0.60 m behind the torus plane so it is plainly visible through the 1.07 m inner opening. It must remain clearance-only scenery, not a disguised guide.
route_and_camera.gate: Opening is 1.78 m wide x 1.72 m high. The panel starts closed across the route, raises about its upper hinge to a 74 degree supported stop, and leaves at least 0.15 m all-around torus passage clearance at its widest orientation.

camera.look_at_path: follow [-2.7,-0.2,2.35] to [1.25,0.65,1.75] while retaining gate and lower curve
camera.rule: No camera cut or fast pan during latch release or opening traversal; the torus hole, trigger, gate, and capture stay readable.

beats.physical_cause: Gravity on the descending banked rail and static contact friction accelerate the torus while its axle rotation changes at v/r. The rail, guards, and columns visibly supply the constraint.
beats.measurement_required: Falsify if the contact speed and axial angular speed fail the no-slip relation within the stated numerical tolerance, if a keyframed yaw substitutes for rolling, or if the track's reaction becomes tensile.

beats.physical_cause: The rolling hoop strikes the finite paddle. Its measured impulse withdraws the latch; only then does the visible counterweight/cable convert gravitational potential into gate rotation. The hoop does not pass through a panel animated out of its way.
beats.measurement_required: Falsify if the latch opens before contact or below 0.23 N s, the gate moves while locked, the gate torque/weight path is absent, or passage at 3.70-4.15 s lacks a positive 0.15 m clearance envelope.

beats.physical_cause: The long, broad lower curve dissipates rolling energy before the torus meets the cork-faced U cradle. The cradle transfers normal force through a visible base rather than freezing the hoop.
beats.measurement_required: Falsify if the torus clips the finite rail/cradle, receives a speed reset, or fails to sustain linear speed <0.02 m/s and angular speed <0.04 rad/s for 0.75 s by the terminal window.

ending: At 9.40-10.20 s the cobalt torus rests upright in the lower-right cradle, its central hole still visible. The gate rests against its open stop and the counterweight is supported; neither object remains in unmotivated motion.
notes: No near-miss is claimed. The rail observed through the central hole is deliberately a positive-clearance static element. Required backend controls include no-slip rolling with finite torus geometry, latch-disabled gate stability, real trigger impulse, open-gate sweep clearance, and compliant terminal capture.
